problems.title: The disk maximizes area at fixed constant width
problems.statement_md: Prove $A(K)\leq\pi w^2/4$ for a planar convex body of constant width $w>0$, with equality only for a disk. You may use the planar isoperimetric inequality.
problems.hint_md: Combine the fixed perimeter supplied by Barbier’s theorem with the isoperimetric inequality.

problems.title: The convex angle function behind inner parallel sets
problems.statement_md: Fix $0<t\leq1-1/\sqrt3$, put $q=1-t$, and define $\alpha_t(x)=\arcsin(\sin x/q)-x$ for $0\leq x\leq\pi/6$. Prove that it is strictly increasing and strictly convex, that $\alpha_t(0)=0$, and that $\alpha_t(x)\leq x$. What happens at $t=0$?
problems.hint_md: Differentiate the arcsine expression twice. To prove the upper bound, compare $\sin x/q$ with $\sin(2x)$ on the stated interval.

problems.title: Concentrating an angle budget
problems.statement_md: Let $a>0$ and $f:[0,a]\to\mathbb R$ be convex with $f(0)=0$. For a finite list $x_1,\ldots,x_N$, if $0\leq x_i\leq a$ and $\sum_i x_i\leq ma$ for an integer $m\geq1$, and $f(a)\geq0$, prove $\sum_i f(x_i)\leq m f(a)$. When $f$ is strictly convex and increasing, characterize equality.
problems.hint_md: The graph of a convex function lies below the chord joining $(0,0)$ and $(a,f(a))$. Apply that bound to each summand.

problems.title: A short perimeter comparison before an arc disappears
problems.statement_md: Let a unit disk polygon have arc angles $\theta_i$ and turning angles $\beta_i\in[0,\pi/3]$, with $\sum\theta_i\geq\pi$. Suppose its erosion $D_{-t}=\{x:x+tB\subset D\}$ at $0\leq t\leq1-1/\sqrt3$ retains all arcs and satisfies $P(D_{-t})=(1-t)[\sum\theta_i-2\sum\alpha_t(\beta_i/2)]$. Prove $P(D_{-t})\geq P(T_{-t})$, where $T$ is the width-one Reuleaux triangle. The displayed formula is an explicit hypothesis here.
problems.hint_md: Total turning bounds the sum of the corner angles. Apply the angle-budget inequality to $f(\beta)=2\alpha_t(\beta/2)$.

problems.title: Integrating a perimeter comparison backwards
problems.statement_md: Let $T$ be the width-one Reuleaux triangle and $r_T=1-1/\sqrt3$. Suppose a convex body $K$ has inradius at least $r_T$ and $P(K_{-t})\geq P(T_{-t})$ for $0\leq t<r_T$. Using absolute continuity of inner-parallel areas and $\frac{d}{dt}A(K_{-t})=-P(K_{-t})$ almost everywhere, prove $A(K_{-t})\geq A(T_{-t})$ for $0\leq t\leq r_T$.
problems.hint_md: Consider the difference of the two eroded areas and integrate its derivative backwards from $r_T$, where the triangle’s remaining area is zero.

problems.title: A mixed-area proof of Blaschke–Lebesgue
problems.statement_md: Using the circumscribed-hexagon theorem and monotonicity of mixed area, prove that every planar convex body of constant width $w>0$ satisfies $A(K)\geq(\pi-\sqrt3)w^2/2$. Exhibit an attaining body. You may use $A(K+L)=A(K)+2A(K,L)+A(L)$.
problems.hint_md: Place the circumscribed hexagon at the origin, so it contains both $K$ and $-K$. Expand the area of $K+(-K)$ and use mixed-area monotonicity.

problems.title: Which curvature perturbations preserve a closed constant-width curve?
problems.statement_md:
First show that every planar constant-width-one support function is $C^{1,1}$. You may use the distributional characterization: for a continuous periodic support function $h$, $h''+h$ is a nonnegative finite measure; conversely, this nonnegativity characterizes support functions. Combine it with $h(\theta+\pi)+h(\theta)=1$.

Let $u(\theta)=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ and $\rho\in L^\infty(0,2\pi)$ be periodic. Show that $\rho=h''+h$ for a periodic $C^{1,1}$ support function of width one if and only if
$$0\leq\rho\leq1,\quad \rho(\theta+\pi)=1-\rho(\theta),\quad \int_0^{2\pi}\rho(\theta)u(\theta)\,d\theta=0.$$
The inequalities and curvature identities are understood almost everywhere. Explain why subtracting first harmonics from a proposed curvature perturbation repairs its moments but need not preserve $0\leq\rho\leq1$.
problems.hint_md: Integrate against sine and cosine. For sufficiency solve $h''+h=\rho$ by variation of constants and examine $h(\theta)+h(\theta+\pi)$.

sources.locator: §3, equation (3.1) and the perturbation preceding Lemma 3.4; admissibility checked explicitly

problems.title: Area is strictly concave along nontranslation width-preserving segments
problems.statement_md:
For periodic $C^{1,1}$ functions $h,f$, let $A(h)=\frac12\int_0^{2\pi}(h^2-h'^2)$. If $f(\theta+\pi)=-f(\theta)$, prove
$$A(h+tf)=A(h)+t\int_0^{2\pi}h(f''+f)+\frac{t^2}{2}\int_0^{2\pi}(f^2-f'^2).$$
Show the last integral is nonpositive, and vanishes precisely for $f=a\cos\theta+b\sin\theta$. If the first harmonics of $f$ vanish, prove $\int f'^2\geq9\int f^2$. Interpret these statements for an admissible segment of width-one bodies.
problems.hint_md: Expand the quadratic form and use the Fourier modes allowed by antipodal oddness.

sources.locator: §2, area formula; §3 variational framework; Fourier companion

problems.title: An area minimizer has curvature radius zero or one almost everywhere
problems.statement_md: Suppose $h$ minimizes area among width-one bodies, and put $\rho=h''+h$. Prove $\rho\in\{0,1\}$ almost everywhere. If the set where $0<\rho<1$ has positive measure, construct a nonzero bounded perturbation $g$ supported where $\varepsilon\leq\rho\leq1-\varepsilon$, antipodally odd and with both first moments zero. Three disjoint measurable patches in a half-circle suffice. Explain why this alone does not prove that the minimizer is a finite Reuleaux polygon.
problems.hint_md: Three patch coefficients satisfy only two homogeneous moment equations. Apply both signs of the perturbation and the strict second variation.

problems.title: A two-moment optimization lemma produces a switching function
problems.statement_md:
Let $f$ be continuous on $[0,\pi]$. Minimize $\int_0^\pi fq$ over measurable $|q|\leq1$ satisfying $\int_0^\pi qu=0$, where $u=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$. Prove that there exists $a\in\mathbb R^2$ such that every minimizer satisfies
$$q(\theta)=-\operatorname{sign}(f(\theta)-a\cdot u(\theta))$$
almost everywhere on the set where $f-a\cdot u\ne0$. You may use the convex subgradient formula
$$\partial_a\int|f-a\cdot u|=\left\{-\int\sigma u:\ |\sigma|\leq1,\ \sigma=\operatorname{sign}(f-a\cdot u)\text{ off its zero set}\right\}.$$
All integrals here are over $[0,\pi]$.
problems.hint_md: Minimize the convex function $F(a)=\int|f-a\cdot u|$ and use a zero subgradient to construct an admissible optimizer.

problems.title: Deriving the switching rule without losing the closure constraints
problems.statement_md:
Let $h$ minimize area among width-one supports and $\rho=h''+h$. Using the two-moment lemma, show that a translation $H=h-a\cdot u$ can be chosen so that
$$H>\tfrac12\ \Longrightarrow\ \rho=0,\qquad H<\tfrac12\ \Longrightarrow\ \rho=1\quad\text{a.e.}$$
Do not assume in advance that the appropriate translation is the Steiner-point normalization.
problems.hint_md: First minimize the first variation over all feasible curvature radii. On a half-circle write $q=2\rho-1$.

problems.title: Equal endpoint slopes force equal arcs
problems.statement_md: Let $H$ be a width-one $C^{1,1}$ support, not identically $1/2$, satisfying $H''+H=0$ a.e. where $H>1/2$, and $H''+H=1$ a.e. where $H<1/2$. Prove that these regions alternate in intervals of one common length $\ell=\pi/N$, where $N\geq3$ is odd. Deduce that the curve is a regular Reuleaux $N$-gon. Compute the endpoint slopes on an interval of length $\ell$.

problems.title: Assembling the support-function variational proof
problems.statement_md:
Use existence of a least-area width-one body, the switching rule, and its ODE classification to prove the Blaschke–Lebesgue theorem, including uniqueness up to rigid motions. You may use
$$A(R_N)=\frac{\pi-N\tan(\pi/(2N))}{2}\quad(N\geq3\text{ odd})$$
for regular Reuleaux polygons. Verify directly that these areas strictly increase with $N$.
problems.hint_md: The disk is not a minimizer. Reduce to the regular polygons and differentiate $\tan x/x$.

problems.title: The normal integral of a circular arc
problems.statement_md:
Let a unit-circle arc have endpoint outward normals $u,v$ and angle $0<\ell<\pi$. Prove
$$\int_\Gamma n\,ds=\tan(\ell/2)(u+v).$$
For a smoothly moving intersection of unit disks with unchanged active arcs, whose centers move with velocities $z_i$, deduce
$$A'(0)=\sum_i z_i\cdot\tan(\ell_i/2)(u_i+v_i).$$
You may use the area shape derivative $A'=\int_{\partial K}V\cdot n\,ds$.
problems.hint_md: Integrate the sine and cosine components about the middle normal. A moving center contributes normal velocity $z_i\cdot n$.

problems.title: A Blaschke motion moves two vertices, not one
problems.statement_md:
Let $n=2k+1\geq5$, with strictly nondegenerate width-one Reuleaux vertices $p_i$ in counterclockwise order, indexed modulo $n$. The arc centered at $p_i$ has normals $u_i=p_{i+k}-p_i$, $v_i=p_{i-k}-p_i$ and angle $\ell_i\in(0,\pi/3)$. Assume all other vertex-pair distances are strictly below one. Rotate $p_i$ counterclockwise about fixed $p_{i-k}$ at unit angular speed, and let $p_j$, $j=i+k$, follow the nearby intersection of the unit circles centered at moving $p_i$ and fixed $p_{i-1}$. All other vertices stay fixed. Prove this is a local constant-width motion in both parameter directions, and derive
$$\dot p_i=-Jv_i,\quad \dot p_j=-\frac{\sin\ell_i}{\sin\ell_j}Ju_j,$$
$$A'(0)=\sin\ell_i\left(\tan\frac{\ell_i}{2}-\tan\frac{\ell_j}{2}\right),$$
where $J$ rotates vectors counterclockwise by $\pi/2$.
problems.hint_md: Differentiate the three affected unit-distance constraints. Only two generating centers have nonzero velocity.

problems.title: Equal coupled arcs are unstable under a Blaschke motion
problems.statement_md:
For the preceding two-vertex motion, suppose $\ell_i=\ell_j=L\in(0,\pi/3)$. Prove
$$\ell_i'=1-2\cos L,\qquad \ell_j'=2\cos L-1,$$
and hence
$$A''(0)=2\tan(L/2)(1-2\cos L)<0.$$
Deduce that a strictly nondegenerate Reuleaux polygon with at least five arcs cannot be a local area minimum, even when its first variation vanishes.
problems.hint_md: For a moving unit vector $w$, its angular velocity is $(Jw)\cdot\dot w$. Apply this to the four endpoint normals.

problems.title: Why local polygon deformations give a global area bound
problems.statement_md:
Fix an odd $N\geq3$. Prove that the width-one Reuleaux polygons with at most $N$ arcs, translated to contain the origin, form a compact class for Hausdorff distance. You may use their representation as intersections of unit disks centered at their vertices; repeated centers may pad a representation to $N$ centers. Explain why a limit of the intersections is still the intersection of the limiting disks.

Then use the two-sided Blaschke variations and area continuity to prove that the triangle minimizes area in this finite class. Assuming Reuleaux polygons are dense among planar constant-width bodies, pass to the whole class. Explain why a negative first variation alone would leave a gap at regular polygons.
problems.hint_md: Normalize by translation, minimize in the compact finite class, and inspect the actual number of nonzero arcs of a minimizer.

problems.title: The shortest arc controls the opposite replacement chord
problems.statement_md:
In a nontriangular, nondegenerate width-one Reuleaux polygon, let $c,d$ be consecutive vertices with a shortest joining boundary arc, centered at $q$. Let the adjacent arcs $bq$ and $qa$ be centered at $d$ and $c$. Prove $|c-d|\leq|a-b|$. In the cyclic configuration shown in the figure, use
$$\angle aqb=\angle cqa+\angle dqb-\angle cqd.$$
Explain why choosing a shortest arc is equivalent to choosing a shortest adjacent chord.
problems.hint_md: All arcs have radius one and angle at most $\pi/3$. Use the two isosceles triangles at $q$ and the side opposite an angle greater than $\pi/3$.

problems.title: Removing a smallest arc and its opposite corner
problems.statement_md:
Use the notation of the shortest-arc chord lemma. Let $p$ be the intersection of the unit circles about $a,b$ closer to the arc $cd$. Replace the arc $cd$ by arcs $cp,pd$ centered at $a,b$, and replace $bq,qa$ by the single arc $ba$ centered at $p$. Show that this removes two vertices and does not increase area.

You may use the following **geometric surgery and comparison lemma** (Hynd §4, following Yaglom–Boltyanskii 7-20): for a shortest arc the replacement is a convex constant-width curve, tangent to the unchanged boundary at $c,d$; with $s,r\in[p,q]$, $|s-p|=|r-q|=1$, the area lost is the sum of the curvilinear pieces $asq,bsq$, and the area gained is that of $crp,drp$. For the paired pieces, a nonnegative arc excess $\widehat{as}-\widehat{cr}$ gives a nonnegative area excess, increasing with that arc excess; the reflected pair obeys the same comparison function. Arc notation uses the circles centered at $p$ and $q$. The task is to complete the reduction and area comparison from this explicit lemma.
problems.hint_md: The sum of the two arc excesses is nonnegative. If one is negative, compare its deficit with the other excess using monotonicity.

problems.title: Rounding corners while keeping width one
problems.statement_md:
Let $K$ have width one, support $h\in C^{1,1}$, and curvature radius $\rho=h''+h\in[0,1]$. For $\delta>0$ set $K_\delta=(K+\delta B)/(1+2\delta)$. Prove
$$h_\delta=\frac{h+\delta}{1+2\delta},\qquad \rho_\delta=\frac{\rho+\delta}{1+2\delta},\qquad \frac{\delta}{1+2\delta}\leq\rho_\delta\leq\frac{1+\delta}{1+2\delta}.$$
Show $h_\delta\to h$ in $C^1$ and that the normal-angle parametrization has no constant intervals. Does this operation by itself make the boundary infinitely differentiable?
problems.hint_md: Apply support-function addition and scaling. A positive lower curvature radius prevents a whole interval of normals from representing one vertex.

problems.title: Checking the support-function splice in Reuleaux approximation
problems.statement_md:
Let $h$ be a width-one $C^{1,1}$ support and $\gamma=hu+h'u'$. On a partition cell $[a,b]\subset[0,\pi]$, suppose a unit-circle center $z$ and angles $a\leq\phi\leq\psi\leq b$ have been constructed with
$$\gamma(a)=z+u(\phi),\qquad\gamma(b)=z+u(\psi).$$
Define $H=\gamma(a)\cdot u$ on $[a,\phi]$, $H=1+z\cdot u$ on $[\phi,\psi]$, and $H=\gamma(b)\cdot u$ on $[\psi,b]$. Prove the pieces match in value and first derivative, with $H''+H\in\{0,1\}$. Doing this on every cell, extend by $H(\theta+\pi)=1-H(\theta)$. Prove this gives a Reuleaux polygon and, if every cell has length at most $\Delta$, that $\|H-h\|_\infty,\|H'-h'\|_\infty\leq2\Delta$. The existence of centers with the stated angle order is the geometric input to this exercise.
problems.hint_md: The vector identities at the junctions give both matching conditions. Bound the two support values by the distance between their contact points.

problems.title: Passing a polygon area inequality to every constant-width body
problems.statement_md: Assume every width-one body has arbitrarily close Reuleaux-polygon approximations in Hausdorff distance. Combine shortest-arc removal with area continuity to prove $A(K)\geq(\pi-\sqrt3)/2$ for every width-one body. Alternatively, pass to the limit using $C^1$ support convergence and $A(h)=\frac12\int(h^2-h'^2)$. Explain why a sequence of strict inequalities does not alone prove uniqueness of the limiting equality case.

problems.title: Every circumscribed equiangular even-gon has the same perimeter
problems.statement_md:
Let $N\geq4$ be even, $\Delta=2\pi/N$, $n_j=u(\alpha+j\Delta)$, and $h_j=h_K(n_j)$ for a width-$w$ body. Intersect the supporting half-planes $x\cdot n_j\leq h_j$ to obtain $P_N$. Allow zero-length sides at coincident consecutive intersections. Prove
$$\ell_j=\frac{h_{j-1}+h_{j+1}-2\cos\Delta\,h_j}{\sin\Delta},\qquad P(P_N)=Nw\tan(\pi/N).$$
Thus its perimeter is independent of $K$ and orientation. Deduce Barbier’s theorem by refining the normal mesh; you may use perimeter continuity for planar convex bodies.
problems.hint_md: Solve the two neighboring support-line intersections in normal/tangent coordinates, then sum and pair opposite supports.

problems.title: Area of an equiangular polygon is a discrete quadratic form
problems.statement_md:
For the preceding supporting polygon prove
$$A(P_N)=\frac{1}{\sin\Delta}\sum_j h_jh_{j+1}-\cot\Delta\sum_jh_j^2.$$
Write $h_j=w/2+g_j$ with $g_{j+N/2}=-g_j$. Using the discrete Fourier basis, prove
$$A(P_N)\leq\frac{Nw^2}{4}\tan(\pi/N),$$
with equality exactly when the sampled support values, after a translation, are all $w/2$. Does equality for a fixed mesh force the enclosed constant-width body to be a disk?
problems.hint_md: Use $A=\frac12\sum h_j\ell_j$. The Fourier multiplier of the remaining quadratic form is proportional to $\cos(m\Delta)-\cos\Delta$.

problems.title: Sliding three width-one strips: the hexagon area calculation
problems.statement_md:
Take six half-planes with normals $n_j=u(j\pi/3)$ and support numbers $h_{j+3}=w-h_j$. Assume all six constraints are active, allowing zero-length sides. Prove that after translating,
$$h_j=\frac w2+(-1)^jt,\qquad |t|\leq w/6,$$
and compute
$$\ell_j=\frac{w-6(-1)^jt}{\sqrt3},\qquad A=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}w^2-6\sqrt3\,t^2.$$
Identify the maximum and the degenerate endpoint shapes. Explain why the minimum in this larger strip family is not the Blaschke–Lebesgue constant.
problems.hint_md: The three-dimensional space of antipodally odd six-tuples consists of two translation modes and one alternating mode.

problems.title: Why finer supporting polygons recover the original body
problems.statement_md:
Translate a width-$w$ body so $0\in K\subset wB$. Let $P_N$ be the circumscribed equiangular $N$-gon with normal gap $\Delta=2\pi/N<\pi$. Prove
$$P_N\subset w\sec(\Delta/2)B,$$
$$d_H(P_N,K)\leq2w\bigl(1+\sec(\Delta/2)\bigr)\sin(\Delta/4).$$
Deduce area convergence, including along the meshes $N=3\cdot2^m$ used in Yaglom–Boltyanskii's area argument. Explain which additional comparison is needed to obtain the sharp lower area bound from those meshes.
problems.hint_md: Choose a sampled normal closest to a point's radial direction, then one closest to an arbitrary test direction.
